governance.evidence_status: EXPLORATORY. The hypothesis was selected from the same historical panel every score was computed on. Freezing the data does not make it a holdout and writing the preregistration first does not restore independence.
governance.tonight_is_not_evidence: Tonight's realised outcome must not be used to decide whether Candidate B was good. One game of about 47 scorable players cannot separate two appearance models, and reading it as though it could is how a coin flip becomes a validation. The decision is sealed before kickoff; the outcome is recorded and graded under the standing ledger, not fed back into this ruling.

identity.basis_definition: the frozen P3 panel EXTENDED with one zero-opportunity panel-shaped row per union-frame candidate the panel lacks, then appearance_model._walk and p3_features.enrich run over the extension. Every union frame row carries a V1 block afterwards, so block presence is a constant.
identity.featuriser: appearance_r8.featurise sliced to its first 76 columns

feature_name_verification.method: one input perturbed at a time; the SET of columns that move is asserted against the claimed names

reliability_constant_k.definition: within-player variance over between-player variance of player-season appearance rates, players with >= 4 games

clean_rerun.note: the committed file was not overwritten; the rerun wrote to the scratchpad and was compared field by field

P3_train_serve_parity.verdict: PASS on the basis; the tonight-only marginal comparison is reported and is not a basis test at n = 47 from one game

incumbent_for_contrast.note: appearance_r8.predict fills the block for every player at serve, so the column is a constant there and a variable in training. That difference is the train/serve half of the defect.

serve_path_reproduces_training_basis_bit.note: The serve path is _prospective_union; the training basis is the union walk. For a player with one frame row that week the two must agree bit for bit. A player with two rows that week is the declared duplicate-ordinal case.

incumbent_block_presence.note: appearance_r8.predict fills the block for every player at serve, so the column is a constant there and a variable in training. That difference is the train/serve half of the defect.

tonight_only_marginal_comparison.caveat: n = 47 from a single game cluster against 4,163 week-1 training rows from sixty game-weeks. The differences are dominated by which two teams these are. Two of the reported failures -- f_practice_improving and f_practice_worsening -- are an artefact of a zero pooled standard deviation where the two means are identical at 0.0.

known_residual_limits.name: universe is still not the roster
known_residual_limits.detail: a union frame row is panel-or-depth-listed. A player with history who is not depth-listed and does not play still produces no frame row. Closing this needs weekly 53-man roster membership for 2020-2025, which is not in this checkout.

known_residual_limits.name: duplicate player-ordinals
known_residual_limits.detail: appearance_model._walk orders by ord alone, so where a player holds two frame rows at the same (season, week) the first in list order becomes history for the second and its label reaches the second row's features. Present in R7 and R8 identically; Candidate B neither introduces nor repairs it.

measured.why_it_matters: appearance_model._walk orders by ord alone, so where a player holds two rows at the same (season, week) the first in list order becomes history for the second and its label reaches the second row's features. A property of the frozen walk and of the union frame key (s, w, t, pid); present in R7 and R8 identically.

sensitivity.note: Both fits are forward-chained on seasons strictly earlier than 2025 and scored on the same rows, so the only difference is whether the 5.85% duplicate-ordinal cell was in the training set. This is a sensitivity, not a repair: the defect is in the frozen walk's ordering and is present in R7 and R8 identically.

known_residual_limits.name: gameday inactives are not read by any appearance model
known_residual_limits.detail: the official list is applied one layer later, in layers.py. Candidate B does not change that and does not claim to.

measured.finding: No appearance model in this repository reads the official inactive list; it is applied a layer later in layers.py. Candidate B does not change that and does not claim to. What this case measures is whether B's latent for a depth-listed cold-start player is still driven to near one by the leak.
